issue_context.title: Endpoint: printer Failed to update OctoPrint status.   Error: 409 Client Error: CONFLICT for url
issue_context.body:
**Home Assistant release with the issue:**
0.96.5
**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**
Ubuntu, virtualenv
**Component/platform:**
OctoPrint
**Description of problem:**
Endpoint: printer Failed to update OctoPrint status.   Error: 409 Client Error: CONFLICT for url: http://**.**.**.**:5000/api/printer
**Additional information:**
octoprint is installed on the same computer in virtualenv. everything works but the warning is distracting
![Безымянный](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45586414/62456355-e78d3a00-b780-11e9-888a-1bcf63091579.png)

Will

Hello

same error with a Anycubic Chiron (the I3mega doesnt show this error),

Home assistant 0.108.3
This happens if the serial connection is not in the connected state.
Same error : it appears when Home-assistant is started while Octoprint is already running and the printer is off (not connected).

This appears to be 100% normal for any printer not connected via serial. This is a warning; not really an error as I have come to learn.

Tollbringer

110.5 same error here "Endpoint: printer Failed to update OctoPrint status. Error: 409 Client Error: CONFLICT for url: http://my_ip:my_port/api/printer". And it occurs the same way as above, printer turned off, but the PI still running.

> 
> 
> 110.5 same error here "Endpoint: printer Failed to update OctoPrint status. Error: 409 Client Error: CONFLICT for url: http://my_ip:my_port/api/printer". And it occurs the same way as above, printer turned off, but the PI still running.

I was searching to find what was causing this issue. That explains it. Before, the raspberry Pi was feeding 5V to the printer board and it was always on even if the printer was off. I "fixed" it by covering the 5V pin on the USB plug to avoid any issues and now the printer is off. but I didn't link the two things. Thanks
This is normal behavior if the printer can not be reached during bootup, and during the subsequent polling checks. All the SKR series boards do this.

> covering the 5V pin on the USB plug

@J-CMartin , can you please give a few more detail on what you meant when you said “covering the 5V pin on the USB plug” ? Thanks.

I dont really think this bug here is really a bug moreso just an exception that should probably say "printer offline" asides from that there is no loss of functionality.  This error only shows up when the octoprint API cannot be reached.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/octoprint/__init__.py#L249

Can anyone confirm what functionality is broken here asides from their printer being offline?  If it was an uncaught exception I would say there is a bug but its definitely being caught here.  Because it is true the integration failed to update the status of the printer due it being offline.
Confirming that it doesn't affect functionality. It would be nice not to be thrown as an error though since 99% of the time, the printer is going to be offline when HA boots.

review_comments: No need to track this, you can just keep track of `self.available`. If it's set to `False`, log the error, otherwise don't.
I've just wanted to log that only once, that's why the `self.available_error_logged` flag was introduced
But that's the same as when you only log it when `self.available` _changes_ from True to False? That also happens once, after that all subsequent logging is ignored.

I've tried to do it like you've suggested at first, but I found out that there are situations when this won't work, so I've added this extra log guard. When any of those 2 API endpoints(job, printer) is marked as failed before the connection error exception occur, then `self.available` is set to False and the connection error will not be logged. This situation will happen when you have your Octoprint server already running but the printer is offline for example.

If you want I can try look into it more deeply(endpoint and error handling) and make separate PR with changes?
This should be handled by a third party library that raises library specific exceptions. We'd welcome PRs that refactor this integration to use a library. 👍
Just FYI, I'm half way such a library + integration...
Why filter it out, it is only going to get logged once because it's guarded by `self.printer_error_logged` ?

I'm filtering out the 409 http status on Printer Endpoint because Octoprint API returns 409 on any printer status that is not operational(error, offline, etc.). In previous version it caused logging of error msg, every single request, anytime the printer is offline(disconnected in terms of Octoprint). I though that we can make it silent and the printer sensor itself will be set to state `unknown` when the printer is not in operational state.
